segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַפָּסַח שֶׁשְּׁחָטוֹ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ, וְקִבֵּל וְהִלֵּךְ וְזָרַק שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ, אוֹ לִשְׁמוֹ וְשֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ, אוֹ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ וְלִשְׁמוֹ — פָּסוּל.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» «The Paschal lamb that» the priest «slaughtered not for its» own «purpose,» i.e., at the time of slaughter he said that his intent was to slaughter it as a different offering, e.g., a peace-offering or burnt-offering, rather than as a Paschal lamb; or if the priest «received» the blood, or «carried» the blood to the altar, or «sprinkled» the blood on the altar while saying that it was «not for the purpose» of the Paschal lamb; «or» if the priest performed the rites both «for its» own «purpose and not for its» own «purpose; or not for its» own «purpose and for its» own «purpose;» in all these cases, the Paschal lamb is «disqualified.»

segments.he: כֵּיצַד לִשְׁמוֹ וְשֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ? לְשֵׁם פֶּסַח וּלְשֵׁם שְׁלָמִים. שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ וְלִשְׁמוֹ — לְשֵׁם שְׁלָמִים וּלְשֵׁם פֶּסַח.
segments.en: «How» does one perform the rites «for its» own «purpose and not for its» own «purpose?» It is in a case where the priest said that his intent is «for the purpose of the Paschal lamb and for the purpose of a peace-offering.» And how does one perform rites «not for its» own «purpose and for its» own «purpose?» It is in a case where the priest says that the offering is «for the purpose of a peace-offering and for the purpose of a Paschal lamb.»

moves.summary: The mishna rules that a Paschal lamb with improper or mixed intent in any of its rites is disqualified.
The mishna defines the two orders of mixed intent: Paschal then peace-offering, and peace-offering then Paschal.

positions.claim: a Paschal lamb slaughtered, received, carried or sprinkled not for its own purpose, or for its own and not its own purpose in either order, is disqualified
